restatement: Give the repository a small, dependency-free node:test runner so the two later bug cards (nested FOR losing outer variables, ?? defaults containing a pipe) can each show a regression test failing first. `npm run test:node` must compile nodes/ and test-node/ with the repo's own tsc into a git-ignored build directory, run the compiled tests with node:test, print TAP on stdout, and exit 0 on pass and nonzero on a test failure or a tsc error. It must not touch tests/, nodes/, jest.config.js or __mocks__/, and may add no dependency other than @types/node.
brief_mismatch: Three minor inconsistencies, none of which blocks the review. (1) The card's Scope table lists scripts/run-node-tests.test.mjs as an edit, but the packet treats it as frozen and the manifest omits it. (2) The card lists scripts/run-node-tests.mjs as an add, while the manifest and diff show an edit of a stub. (3) c1 is worded around `npm run test:node`, but the frozen tests invoke the script directly, so the npm script wiring and the clean-clone `npm ci` path in spec.md's Goal are covered by no test and can only be judged from the diff.
verification_plan: c1: package.json has a test:node script pointing at the runner; the runner calls the repo's own tsc with -p tsconfig.test.json and then node --test over the compiled test-node/**/*.test.js.
c1: the runner's exit status is the node --test child's status (0 on pass, nonzero on fail), with no path that swallows a failure or a null status.
c1 / brief Q2: a nonzero tsc status exits the runner nonzero before any test is spawned.
c1: with file arguments the runner runs exactly those files, as the frozen failing-file test requires; with none it discovers the compiled tests recursively.
c2 / brief Q1: the reporter is forced to tap, the child's stdout reaches the runner's stdout, nothing is printed before 'TAP version' on a passing run, and a failing test yields a 'not ok' line.
c2: the runner still emits TAP when itself run under an outer node --test, as the frozen tests do.
c3: .gitignore contains the build output directory and it matches tsconfig.test.json outDir.
c3 / m1: the diff touches nothing under tests/, nodes/, jest.config.js or __mocks__/, and the frozen test file is unchanged.
m2: package.json adds only @types/node as a devDependency, and package-lock.json is consistent with it so `npm ci` on a clean clone installs it.
brief Q3 / spec constraint: spawn uses argv with no shell, launches via process.execPath, and builds paths with path.join/resolve.
Rubric: runner under 60 lines, imports only node built-ins plus the typescript binary; smoke test asserts a rendered string through lexer, parser and interpreter.
Cycle goal: no stale build output or discovery behaviour that could give a bug card a false 'fails first' or false pass reading.
f1: the build directory is cleared before compiling.

findings.title: package-lock.json change is one root line and looks hand-edited, so the diff does not show that `npm ci` on a clean clone installs @types/node

serves.scenario: tsconfig.test.json sets "types": ["node"], so the runner depends on node_modules/@types/node being installed. The lock diff adds only the root devDependencies line: no node_modules/@types/node package entry is added or changed, against the card's estimate of about 20 lines. The lock's root block still lists @types/jest and jest, which package.json's devDependencies do not, and a real `npm install` would have rewritten that block. If the lock has no hoisted @types/node entry satisfying ^24.10.2, `npm ci` either refuses the out-of-sync lock or leaves the types missing; tsc then fails with TS2688 and every later bug card gets a nonzero exit with no TAP, so none can show a test failing first. I cannot see the rest of the lock, so this is unconfirmed; the reproduction settles it either way.

findings.rubric: c1 (tr-01: npm run test:node compiles and runs, exiting 0 when tests pass), read with spec.md's Goal: 'on a clean clone after npm ci'
findings.reproduction: 1. Clone head 0e1a6b4 into an empty directory with no node_modules. 2. Run `npm ci`. 3. Run `npm run test:node`. Expected: exit 0 and stdout starting 'TAP version'. The finding holds if step 2 errors on a package.json/lock mismatch, or step 3 fails with 'Cannot find type definition file for node'. It is refuted if both succeed. Smallest fix if it holds: regenerate the lock with `npm install --package-lock-only` and commit the result.

findings.title: With no compiled tests and no arguments, the runner calls `node --test` with no files, which falls back to default discovery and re-enters the runner

serves.scenario: If test-node/ compiles to zero *.test.js files, `files` is empty and `node --test --test-reporter=tap` runs its default discovery from the repo root. That matches scripts/run-node-tests.test.mjs, which spawns the runner three times, recursively. It cannot happen while smoke.test.ts exists, so it is noted for the lead only; a guard exiting nonzero on an empty list would close it.

findings.rubric: spec.md Runner interface: with no arguments it runs every .test-build/test-node/**/*.test.js
findings.reproduction: Remove every *.test.ts under test-node/ but keep a non-test .ts file there so the directory still compiles, then run `node scripts/run-node-tests.mjs`. The runner executes scripts/run-node-tests.test.mjs instead of reporting zero tests.
